question: In the experimental matrix of sewage sludge co-incineration in a fluidized bed, which runs vary the bed particle size, and to what sizes?
rendered:
According to the excerpt from [Co-Incineration of Real Municipal Sewage Sludge in a Fluidized Bed: Effects of the Coexistence of P, Fe, and Na on Agglomeration and Heavy Metal Emissions, page 2], the experimental variables included the incineration temperature, gas velocity, bed particle size, and P, Na, and Fe ratios.

The excerpt from [Co-Incineration of Real Municipal Sewage Sludge in a Fluidized Bed: Effects of the Coexistence of P, Fe, and Na on Agglomeration and Heavy Metal Emissions, page 4] states: "Figure 3. Effects of operating gas velocity and bed material particle size on defluidization time: (a) operating gas velocity; (b) particle size of bed material."

The excerpt from [Co-Incineration of Real Municipal Sewage Sludge in a Fluidized Bed: Effects of the Coexistence of P, Fe, and Na on Agglomeration and Heavy Metal Emissions, page 4] also mentions: "An increase in the bed material particle size led to a corresponding decrease in the defluidization time."

However, the specific sizes of the bed particles are mentioned in the excerpt from [Co-Incineration of Real Municipal Sewage Sludge in a Fluidized Bed: Effects of the Coexistence of P, Fe, and Na on Agglomeration and Heavy Metal Emissions, page 6]: "The 545 μm bed particles provide better fluidity at the same gas velocity, which results in superior operational stability and a longer defluidization time."

The excerpt from [Co-Incineration of Real Municipal Sewage Sludge in a Fluidized Bed: Effects of the Coexistence of P, Fe, and Na on Agglomeration and Heavy Metal Emissions, page 3] mentions: "Figure 3b shows the defluidization time for three different bed material particle sizes. An increase in the bed material particle size led to a corresponding decrease in the defluidization time. Given that several parameters were fixed in this study, 650 μm was selected as the primary particle size, and the gas velocity was set to 1.3× Umf for the 650 μm bed at 800 °C."

Therefore, the bed particle sizes that vary in the experimental matrix are 545 μm, 650 μm, and 775 μm.
